title: Wuchebehsuck (Montauk North Neck)
summary: A Montauk North Neck valley name associated with a small pond outlet and the 1670 Montauk deed.
introduction_content: Wuchebehsuck is a valley on the east side of North Neck at Montauk in East Hampton town.
history_content: The place was connected with a seasonal outlet from a small flaggy pond and swamp, and with the tract later remembered as the Wuchebehsuck purchase, nine-score acre purchase, or land between the ponds.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as "a brook" or "outlet of a pond," and compared with a related Connecticut form.

Why Place Names Matter

“The overlap of place names tells a nuanced story of territory and presence.”

— Native Places Atlas, University of Utah American West Center, Native Places: An Indigenous Atlas of Utah and the Intermountain West (2025), Project description, paragraph 2
preservation_content: Wuchebehsuck preserves a Montauk landscape name tied to water, valley geography, and a 1670 deed. The deed does not establish the exact modern boundaries or valley location.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement on Montauk North Neck, based on the described east-side valley and pond outlet. Coordinates are approximate and not exact deed boundaries.
